correctness.rationale: The exact error after ordered row picks i,j is ||e||^2-ai^2-(aj-cij ai)^2. For two rows F12-F21=c^2(d^2-a^2) establishes choosing the initially larger residual first is the better of the only two nonrepeating sequences, and the p-weight of that first row grows monotonically; p=0 allows repeated rows and can only worsen conditional error. Degenerate residual-zero and equal-residual cases are handled. For the 3x3 rational full-rank example, independent exact reconstruction verifies unit rows, determinant 13/27, all nine Fij entries, uniform mean 65572/6561, first-row-2 probability at p=40 greater than 100/101 and conditional second-step error 7748/729. This gives the strict lower bound >21/2 while first-step expected decrease increases with p. No longer-horizon or positive-sparsity-regularization claim is made.

value.rationale: It determines a sharp and surprising smallest-row-count boundary where a seemingly beneficial adaptive row-sampling rule can worsen actual two-step error, despite improving the first-step conditional expected error. This gives a concrete methodological caution for finite-horizon iterative solvers, not a trivial restatement of convergence rate.

final_claim: For exactly two linearly independent unit rows, residual-power sampling gives nonincreasing two-update unconditional mean squared error as exponent p increases on (0,infinity), never exceeding p=0 uniform sampling; a specific rational three-row system has E40>21/2>10>E0=65572/6561 despite one-step improvement.
limitations: An unlocated stochastic ordering of the two-step conditional projection distribution might cover the two-row statement.
The finite counterexample is exact but one three-row system; it does not settle optimal exponents for broader matrix classes or longer horizons.
